the relationship between migrants and host country legal systems is not a simple one.

the legal adaptations of migrants in the host countries are a result of a complex interplay between the legal system of the host country, the migrant’s own cultural background, and the social and economic conditions of the host country and the migrants.
migrants are not only legal actors in the sense that they are bound by law, but that they also have an agency to shape the law.
The main takeaway from our work is that
migrants are not only adapting to their host countries, but they are also adapting the legal system to suit their needs.
migrants' relationship with law is a complex and dynamic phenomenon.
